tail:
### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: step 4.1 / Proof
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: “∅ is open hence a Gδ by [L4]”
WHY IT FAILS: [L4] only records that ∅ is open (via [[def-metric-topology]] and [[def-topological-space]]); it does not state that every open set is a Gδ. The conclusion that an open set is a Gδ requires the (trivial) observation that an open set is the intersection of the constant sequence of itself — a fact contained in the definition of Gδ rather than in [L4]. The inference is therefore not licensed by [L4] alone. A competent reader fills this gap immediately, so the defect is non‑fatal.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Cite the Gδ definition or add a phrase like “(every open set is a Gδ by the constant sequence)”.

### FINDING 2 — NONFATAL — location: step 7.1 / Proof
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: “and it is T3, T_{2½}, T2, T1 and T0 by the implications already proved on this page”
WHY IT FAILS: The page does **not** contain proofs of the implications that a completely regular T1 space (T_{3½}) is regular (hence T3), or that T3 implies T_{2½} implies T2 implies T1 implies T0. The statement that these are “already proved on this page” is false. The mathematical conclusions are nevertheless correct (completely regular ⇒ regular is immediate by taking preimages of intervals, and the rest of the chain is supplied by [[lem-urysohn-sits-between-hausdorff-and-regular-plus-t1]] and elementary facts), so the defect is non‑fatal.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Replace with a proper citation of the relevant hierarchy lemma, or briefly note the standard arguments.
